jobs.title: Director, Product Management
jobs.description:
Who We're Looking For:
We are looking for a Director of Product Management to lead a team of PMs as well as own the product strategy for empowering developers on the Now platform to build and take their applications to production faster. These areas include developer reach, testing, sandboxing, metering, and deployment of AI and human generated code.
As agentic build tools compress the time it takes to author a change, the bottleneck moves downstream. Testing and deploying safely to production is already one of the loudest customer asks and one of the sharpest pain points on the platform. When changes originate from agents as well as people, and arrive at a much higher rate, the ability to validate and trust them quickly stops being a quality-of-life improvement and becomes a precondition for platform growth. You will lead the team that enables this for developers.
This is not four adjacent feature areas with a shared manager. Customers experience the SDLC as one motion, and the central product challenge of this role is the connective tissue: a sandbox that behaves like the instance you will deploy to, a test suite that knows what changed, a release path that carries the evidence, and a model for building directly in production that an admin can actually govern. You set the strategy that makes their roadmaps resolve into a single lifecycle rather than four products that ship past each other.
The scope is deeply technical and close to execution. The Developer Reach feature area alone unlocks a path to building in production that admins can manage at scale without losing control, and it demands real technical depth to steer. You will also carry a broad surface, over twenty product areas, with the escalation volume that comes with it, and you will need to run that operational load without letting it consume the strategic work.
What you get to do in this role:
- Own the multi-year product strategy and roadmap across Developer Reach, Developer Sandboxes, Agentic Testing, and Release Ops, and define how they compose into one lifecycle from authored change to governed, audited deployment.

- Build, lead, and develop a team of PMs, one per area. Set a clear standard for product craft, coach PMs on strategy and execution, and hold the bar on the seams between them: shared primitives, consistent models, and a single coherent customer narrative.

- Set product direction for validating AI-originated change at scale: what it means to trust an agent's output, what evidence a release needs to carry, and how much of the test and review burden can be automated without losing accountability.

- Drive the Developer Reach strategy, including the product model for building in production with admin control, guardrails, and reversibility at enterprise scale.

- Define the sandbox strategy: provisioning speed, production parity, data handling, and the developer experience of getting a safe place to work in seconds rather than days.

- Own the release governance path end to end, including the tradeoffs between developer velocity and auditability, and the gating model that makes those tradeoffs explicit rather than accidental.

- Shape the metering and cost-modeling strategy for this area in partnership with Pricing & Packaging and Finance, and understand how it impacts the entire App Engine portfolio.

- Build the triage discipline that keeps escalations across a broad product surface from displacing the roadmap.

- Model an AI-first way of working: use agentic coding tools directly, build and deploy against your own products, and bring firsthand experience of the pain your customers are describing.
To be successful in this role you have:
- Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI's potential impact on the function or industry.

- 12+ years of product management experience, including experience leading and growing a team of PMs, with a track record of setting technical strategy independently rather than executing a roadmap someone else defined.

- A track record of developing PMs, raising the bar on product thinking and execution across a team, and growing earlier-career PMs into strong owners of their areas.

- Deep experience owning developer platform, DevOps, or SDLC products at enterprise scale: CI/CD, test automation, environment management, release orchestration, or change management.

- Genuine hands-on technical comfort, including reading code, reasoning about system architecture, and holding your own in design discussions with senior engineers. Direct, regular personal use of AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Windsurf in your own workflow.

- Experience with enterprise change-management or release-governance systems and the tradeoffs between developer velocity and auditability, ideally including systems that gate deployment through a controlled artifact such as a change set.

- Ideally, experience with test strategy at scale: automated test generation, coverage and flakiness economics, regression management, and what it takes for a team to actually trust a green build.

- Familiarity with environment and infrastructure provisioning models, ephemeral environments, production parity, and data seeding or masking, and the cost and security tradeoffs each carries.

- Working knowledge of agentic development workflows and what changes when a meaningful share of commits originate from an agent rather than a person: review, attribution, validation, and rollback.

- Proven ability to build and defend an executive-level strategic case, and to navigate cross-business-unit governance and ownership disputes at the VP and SVP level, driving alignment across genuinely contested boundaries.

- Demonstrated ability to run a high-volume operational surface, triaging escalations and production issues across many product areas while continuing to ship against a multi-year strategy.

- Exceptional written and verbal communication, able to translate deep technical tradeoffs into a strategy that lands with engineers and with executive stakeholders in the same conversation.

Why join us?
- Own the part of the platform that decides whether agentic development is safe enough for enterprises to adopt, at the moment that question is being answered.

- Take four high-stakes bets that are currently separate and make them feel like one product, with the mandate and the team to actually do it.

- Drive the Developer Reach strategy for bringing agentic development on the Now platform to any developer in an organization, and the broader production-build model, one of the most technically ambitious efforts in the org and a direct answer to a long-standing customer ask.

- Operate at the center of the Platform Agentic Build Lifecycle org during the shift to AI-native software development, with influence over how changes get tested, governed, and released rather than only how they get written.

- Grow a team of PMs at the point where the platform’s velocity ceiling is actually set.

Autonomous agents are moving from research to production. This role puts you at the center of that shift. Your product decisions will shape how the next generation of autonomous work gets done across large organizations.

- Engage directly with code: review implementations, stand up demos, and validate feasibility alongside engineering.
- Use hands-on experimentation to de-risk product bets and accelerate time-to-market.
- Stay at the leading edge of agentic AI, autonomous agents, open-source frameworks, orchestration patterns, memory architectures, and translate that into concrete product capabilities.

Own the product surface area and platform primitives
- Define and drive the product's long-term vision: autonomous agents enterprises trust to do real work, from desktop execution to orchestrated workflows across systems.
- Architect the roadmap for agentic platform capabilities: orchestration, memory and context management, action execution, endpoint interaction, and secure agent governance.
- Translate emerging agent patterns into scalable platform primitives that can be leveraged across this product and other ServiceNow AI offerings.
- Partner with frontier AI teams and the open-source ecosystem to bring state-of-the-art capabilities into enterprise production.

Own adoption and measurable outcomes at scale
- Define clear adoption paths and usage models for agentic capabilities across customer segments.
- Partner with go-to-market and outbound teams to ensure time-to-value and measurable impact.
- Establish metrics early. Task completion rates, success rates, latency, cost per action, and iterate rapidly against them.
- Engage with external ecosystem players and partners as needed to accelerate roadmap and adoption.
- Balance near-term customer deliverables with long-term platform differentiation and governance innovation.
Builder with hands-on technical depth
- You don't just define products. You build, test, and iterate.
- 12+ years of product management experience, recent hands-on experience shipping agentic products in the last 12–18 months. Years of PM tenure matter far less than what you've shipped recently and how deep you've gone technically.

Agentic AI expertise and frontier AI fluency

- Hands-on involvement with LLM fine-tuning, prompt engineering at scale, or domain-specific model development.

Moveworks, now part of ServiceNow, is building the agentic AI layer that sits between every employee and the systems they rely on. This is a senior, highly technical IC role for someone who has spent most of their career running infrastructure, platform modernization, or large-scale distributed systems programs. You will manage the program — directly, end to end — and your influence will come from technical depth, sharp judgment, and an ability to align engineering leaders, executives, and partner organizations around a single execution plan. As the Moveworks BU scope expands, so will yours.
What you get to do in this role:
- Own the Moveworks Infrastructure portfolio of strategic and technical initiatives. Your primary focus will be to drive the roadmap and execution plans for Moveworks Infrastructure initiatives; as you scale you will also take over from engineering infra operational processes like capacity planning and budgeting
- Focus on initiatives expanding MW Infra footprint . We are moving to a tri-cloud + on-prem + SPC strategy where we need to develop the tools and process for managing our infra stack across diverse environments. Align any ambiguous strategic direction into concrete milestones, dependencies, and decision points.
- Run the program, not the people . As the TPM, you will be the connective tissue across engineering, product, design, security, GTM, finance, and field organizations — driving outcomes through clarity, structured decision-making, and relentless follow-through.
- Identify and resolve technical misalignment . Spot misalignment across teams, architectures, and roadmaps early — before it becomes a delivery risk — and partner with engineering leads to drive resolution quickly. Lead architecture reviews, surface cross-system risks (latency budgets, blast radius, multi-tenancy, AI safety, evals), and broker tradeoffs between engineering teams.
- Build the operating system for the program . Status, risk, scope, and decision logs that engineering directors and VPs actually read. Quarterly planning rhythms that reflect reality. Executive narratives that are honest about where things stand.
- Be the senior partner to engineering leadership . Pair directly with Distinguished Engineers, VPs of Engineering, and product leaders. Represent the program to the CTO, CPO, and executive staff. Own the message.
- Define TPM excellence . As we grow and expand our TPM team, you will serve as the model for how to operate. Set the standard for what senior technical program management looks like at Moveworks, mentor TPMs across the org without being their manager, and codify the patterns that scale.
Required:
- 12+ years of technical program management experience , with most of that time spent on infrastructure, platform, cloud, reliability, developer productivity, or modernization programs. You have operated at staff, principal, or director IC scope on programs where the hard part was not coordination alone, but understanding technical dependencies, sequencing migrations, managing reliability risk, and helping engineering leaders make durable tradeoffs.
- Deep technical fluency across infrastructure modernization domains — distributed systems, cloud-native infrastructure, Kubernetes, multi-region and multi-cloud architectures, hyperscaler platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), identity, data platforms, observability, reliability, and migration strategy. You do not need to be the architect, but you need enough technical depth to pressure-test plans, spot cross-system risk, and earn credibility with senior engineers.
- Background in agentic AI, conversational AI, or AI assistant platforms — you understand why agent runtimes, tool calling, RAG, and evals are not the same problem.
- A track record of leading cross-org programs involving 100+ engineers, multiple VPs, and competing roadmaps — ideally including at least one large-scale integration, migration, or platform unification.
- Excellent written communication . You can compress a 200-engineer program into a one-page exec narrative without losing the truth of it. You write decision docs that hold up under scrutiny.
- Strong technical judgment under ambiguity . You know when to dig in, when to delegate to engineering leads, and when to escalate. You are comfortable saying “this plan won’t work” in a room full of senior leaders.

Strongly Preferred:
- Prior IC senior TPM experience at a hyperscaler, large SaaS platform, or AI-first company.
- Comfort operating across SaaS, on-prem regulated, and government cloud (FedRAMP, IL5) deployment models.
- Experience leading post-acquisition technical integration programs at scale.

What Success Looks Like in the First Year:
- Quarter 1: You have a grasp of the Moveworks replatform roadmap and are driving the execution plan for the first release helping the team address blockers. Engineering leaders across ServiceNow and Moveworks trust your judgment and pull you into the rooms that matter.
- Quarter 2: You are able to scale to drive multiple releases going on in parallel on the Moveworks replatforming roadmap as well as the current infrastructure expansion and improvement initiatives, and proactively surface key risks to the plans and drive the path to mitigation. The executive staff has confidence in the plan because the plan is honest.
- Quarter 3-4: Team has successfully delivered 1 or 2 releases on the roadmap under your leadership; major milestones land on time and at quality, and you are a trusted partner for infrastructure leadership and team

Why This Role:
This role is especially compelling for senior TPMs who have operated in high-scale infrastructure environments and want more ownership than a narrowly-scoped platform program can offer. You will get the scale, technical complexity, and executive visibility of a large technology company, combined with the pace, ambiguity, and scope expansion of a fast-growing AI business unit.
Most senior TPM roles come with a fixed scope and focus on driving meetings and reporting the status. This one is different. It is a seat at the center of the Moveworks BU which is growing at an unprecented rate — your scope will expand as the BU scales. You will be measured by the technical and business outcomes you drive. If you thrive in an environment where you have the agency to move the needle for the company and learn something new every single day, then this role is for you.

CRM Voice AI builds autonomous voice agents for customer service that resolve customer interactions end-to-end and drive significant value for the business. We're a team inside ServiceNow's CRM business unit, shipping production voice AI with enterprise customers today and scaling aggressively. Our agents run on a real-time streaming voice pipeline with best-in-class orchestration, integrated into the same platform where many of our customers already manage their front, middle, and back-office workflows. We work in pods - small, dedicated teams embedded with a single enterprise customer, building their voice agents from first call to self-sufficiency. A pod owns the full lifecycle: agent shadowing, conversation design, build, production go-live, monitoring and optimization and the handoff that makes the customer self-sufficient so the pod can move on to the next one. Each pod pairs forward-deployed engineers with a product manager who owns both the customer outcome and the product learning that comes from it.
Every PM on this team runs at least one pod directly and has visibility across others. You're in the customer's world - on their calls, in their systems, solving their problems - while simultaneously shaping what the product becomes. The learnings from your pods feed directly into the platform roadmap and into repeatable, productized assets that scale beyond any single customer.

- You drive ServiceNow’s conversational experience itself: dialog quality, turn-taking, interruption handling, barge-in behavior, and endpointing. You collaborate directly with the platform voice team on voice pipeline innovation, the low-latency infrastructure that makes a voice agent feel like a conversation rather than a bot reading a script. When the platform team is making stack decisions about real-time streaming, LLM orchestration, or voice-to-voice model integration, you're in the room with production customer data and real-world edge cases.
- You will support customers across our industry verticals. As we scale across customers, you evaluate which patterns, intents, and conversation flows can be productized into out-of-the-box voice content for a specific industry. You're turning one-off wins into repeatable assets, and you have the customer exposure to know which abstractions actually hold.

jobs.title: Staff Inbound Product Manager, AI Specialists and Voice AI
jobs.description:
Zero Touch Support exists to make working with your IT department easy and pain-free.
That is a bigger surface than any one product. It starts at the front door, where Moveworks, Employee Slate, and our chat experiences meet employees inside the tools they already use and resolve most of what they need before a ticket ever exists. When something does need real work, our AI Specialists pick it up, carry it end to end, and close it. Voice AI does the same for the people who would still rather pick up the phone. Employee Insights shows us and our customers where the friction actually sits, so the whole system improves on a loop instead of on a release cycle.
Put together, that is the difference between an employee filing a ticket and waiting, and an employee just getting on with their day.
About the role
You will own a piece of that portfolio outright. What it does, who it is for, what “good” means, and whether we are honestly there yet.
The interesting part of this job is not the model. It is everything around the model. Every customer environment is different: different knowledge quality, different catalog, different naming conventions, different appetite for letting an agent act on its own. An agent that performs great on a clean eval set can behave differently in a live enterprise for reasons that have nothing to do with reasoning ability. Understanding why, and designing for it, is the job.
We treat evaluation as a product surface rather than a QA step. We run production-ready code against real customer data before we ship, we write and tune our own judge prompts, and eval results are our launch criteria.
ServiceNow moves faster than a company our size has any right to. We shipped an autonomous L1 specialist, and the evaluation discipline behind it, in the time most enterprises spend forming a committee. We are not reacting to AI. We are deciding what AI-first, enterprise-grade software actually means, for the largest companies in the world, who run their business on our platform and cannot afford for us to get this wrong. A lot of that definition does not exist yet, which means on many weeks you will be the person framing the problem rather than receiving it.
How we work is changing as fast as what we build. We are AI-native in our own process, not just in what we ship: prototype with AI instead of describing the idea, put a working demo in front of people instead of a slide about a demo, generate the deck, draft the spec, stand up a rough eval harness. ServiceNow invests in state-of-the-art tooling and expects you to use it, so the role itself is being redefined in real time, and product managers are better positioned than anyone to lead that shift and pull an AI-product team forward with them.
We prove products out in the wild before we scale them. That means working forward deployed: embedded with a customer, in their environment, building and tuning against their real data and their real edge cases until the it works. Then the harder half, turning what you learned into something that generalizes to the next thousand customers. At most AI companies those are two different jobs, and the handoff between them is where the insight gets lost. Here it is one person, and it is you.
What you get to do in this role
- Own an AI-Native product end to end, from the customer problem through launch criteria to how it performs in production.
- Deploy forward. Embed with some of the largest IT organizations in the world on problems they have not solved, build in their environment against their real data, then get into the guts of the AI Agent execution logs to understand what is actually happening. Both halves matter. The best insights live in the gap between them.
- Define what “good” means for an autonomous agent, alongside engineering and our AI Quality CoE, then hold the line on it. That includes the hard conversations about what we can defensibly promise a customer and how much value we are actually delivering them.
- Own your outcome metrics and make sure the instrumentation exists to know whether what you shipped moved them.
- Run design partnerships with enterprises betting real service desks on this, and get what you learn back into the roadmap fast.
- Write the strategy, the specs, and the analysis yourself.
- Work AI-native. Use AI tools to prototype, draft, and communicate. Build a working prototype instead of describing one, and set the bar for how the team around you works.
- Coach other product managers. This is a senior role on a small team, so how you raise the people around you counts as much as what you ship.
To be successful in this role you have:
- Have owned an AI-Native product end to end and been the person accountable for its quality bar. For most people this means eight or more years in product management, but we care about the ownership, not the years.
- Have shipped something built on LLMs to paying customers, and understand what enterprise-grade means for AI: the quality bar, the guardrails, the telemetry, and the work of earning a customer’s trust before they hand an agent real work.
- Can do your own analysis. You should be comfortable pulling your own data and understanding how a metric was built before you rely on it.
- Stay curious, and can find the signal in the noise.
- Document your position clearly and justify your approach. Decisions here get made through research and documentation.
- Are willing to own the outcome when the org chart is ambiguous about who should, which happens often.

Preferred qualifications
- Agent evaluation: eval set design, LLM-as-judge, closing the gap between offline results and production behavior.
- Forward-deployed, applied AI, or embedded delivery experience. You have built something inside a customer’s environment and then had to make it work for everyone else.
- IT service management, service desk operations, or enterprise support.
- Voice agents, or conversational products where latency and turn-taking matter.
- Experience taking a product from zero to one, where the users, the quality bar, and the economics all had to be worked out at once.
- AI-native working habits. AI assistants and productivity tools are already part of how you work. You use them to prototype, draft, and analyze, and you have automated enough of your own day-to-day that you spend your time on the judgment calls instead of the mechanics. Bonus if you have changed how a team around you works because of it.
